answer: Marginal Terrace Pricing. Each identity pays a fee equal to a rising function of how many identities already share its referral neighborhood, so the n-th sibling costs roughly n times the first. Attackers issuing many identities from one source face a steepening curve, not a flat toll. Honest users in sparse regions pay little, like early nectar in a thin season. The fee is collected as quartz-denominated credits burned at issuance, so the attacker's per-identity cost grows superlinearly while the marginal honest cost stays flat.
